meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental-Napoleonic tradition with fully integrated EU law; notarial authentication is dispositive for corporate acts)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended by Ley 11/2021, de 9 de julio, and by Ley 6/2023, de 17 de marzo; Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010 approved by Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, in particular Article 43 (Registro de Titulares Reales); Real Decreto-Ley 7/2021, de 27 de abril (transposing EU Directive 2018/843, AMLD5, strengthening the unified UBO register); Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), Articles 4 and 22 (share capital and registry inscription). The competent FIU and AML/CFT supervisory authority is SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias), attached to the Banco de España. UBO identification and declaration duties apply to every Spanish S.L. at incorporation and annually thereafter; obliged professionals must pierce and document the entire chain of ownership of each incorporator.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificado Negativo de Denominación Social (Negative Name Clearance Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued natively in Spain; no apostille or consular legalization required; must be presented to the notary within its validity window

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Current Legal Existence of each foreign corporate shareholder (Certificado de constitución y vigencia / Extracto del registro de origen)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official commercial or companies registry of the foreign shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention certification by the competent authority of the country of origin (Spain is a Hague member since 1978; China accession effective 7 November 2023); consular legalization only for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of the Passport / National Identity Document of each individual incorporator and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing government authority of the individual's home country, notarized in the home country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille where certified copies originate outside Spain; alternatively direct certification before the Spanish notary of originals

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Poder Notarial) granted by foreign shareholders in favor of the Spanish incorporation representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the foreign jurisdiction where the grantor is domiciled
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the competent foreign authority; Spanish notary must assess capacity and post-apostille effect

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificado de vigencia de la sociedad extranjera)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign commercial registry and, where applicable, tax authority of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; original or certified electronic copy with secure verification code acceptable to the Spanish notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: NIE Certificate (Certificado del Número de Identificación de Extranjero) for each non-resident incorporator, administrator, or attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Subdelegación del Gobierno / Spanish Ministry of the Interior
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued internally by the Spanish State; no apostille or consular step required, but the certificate must be current and the underlying passport must be exhibited to the notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs) under Articles 14 and 15 of Ley 10/2010, including family members and known close associates of any PEP; mandatory pre-onboarding screening of every shareholder, director, officer, and ultimate beneficial owner against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the OFAC SDN List (mandatory because target payment rails include USD-denominated Progress Wire and TT transfers routed through correspondent banking), the United Kingdom OFSI consolidated list where relevant, and the Spanish national financial sanctions and terrorist financing designations published through SEPBLAC. Any unresolved match, zero-day sanctions hit, or unexplained PEP connection must terminate the acceptance file or trigger Suspicious Transaction Report (STR/SRO) filing before the notarial deed is signed. Screening results, source-of-funds statements, and corporate structure diagrams must be archived in the client acceptance file and certified by the designated compliance officer at the incorporation law firm.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) — online Solicitud de Certificado Negativo de Denominación Social, accessible through the RMC official portal at https://www.rmc.es and through the notarial electronic filing platform (CUSA / Colegio de Registradores gateway).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Per Article 407 of Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil) and Articles 6–8 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital: the corporate denomination may consist of fantasy words and/or references to the corporate object; it must be written exclusively in Latin-script Roman characters, using the Spanish alphabet (including co-official Spanish languages such as Catalan, Galician, and Basque); foreign-language terms are permitted if transliterated into Latin characters; symbols, drawings, diacritically altered non-Roman scripts, and undefined acronyms are rejected. The registered name of the S.L. must include or be completed by the legal form designator 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.'; any bilingual or transliterated variant must preserve a single official spelling across all company documents.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms that imply national, regional, or local public authority status, such as 'España', 'Estado', 'Gobierno', 'Ministerio', 'Banco de España', 'Instituto Nacional', 'Consejo General del Poder Judicial', 'Ayuntamiento', 'Generalitat', 'Real', or 'Oficial', which require prior authorization from the Council of Ministers, the corresponding ministry, or the competent public body

Terms reserved for regulated financial, insurance, and mutual-guarantee sectors, such as 'Banco', 'Caja', 'Seguros', 'Mutua', 'Sociedad de Garantía Recíproca', requiring prior authorization from the Bank of Spain, Directorate-General of Insurance, or the corresponding sectoral supervisor

Denominations identical to a name already inscribed in the Registro Mercantil Central index or denominations that indicate misleading similarity likely to confuse third parties, prohibited under Article 8 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital
Words or expressions contrary to criminal law, public morality, or public order, and names that falsely suggest a connection with royal, governmental, military, or international bodies
Surnames or personal names of identifiable natural persons without the written consent of the person concerned, or names of legal entities without definitive corporate consent documents
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within one calendar month of the RMC's unfavorable certification notice, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) of the Ministry of the Presidency, Justice and Relations with the Cortes, under Articles 112–115 of Ley 39/2015, identifying the proposed denomination, the RMC case reference number, and the legal grounds contesting any erroneous finding of identity or misleading similarity; alternatively, the applicant may immediately re-file a new negative-name application incorporating a distinctive corporate element (e.g., a geographic descriptor such as 'Iberia', an activity qualifier such as 'Refractarios', or a registered trademark reference) to overcome the similarity objection. The 90-day reservation period is not extendable: if the public deed is not granted within the validity window, the certificate lapses and a fresh application and fee are required; in exceptional cases, a precertification review may be requested from the RMC's Denominations Department without recourse to formal administrative appeal where the rejection is based on formal documentary insufficiency.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally accepted for an S.L. engaged in industrial refractory masonry contracting, provided the virtual office is actually a serviced co-working or registered-agent center with a physical interior, a dedicated workstation or office assigned to the company, physical mail reception, access to official notifications, and a valid lease or service agreement; a pure virtual mailbox without physical premises or administrative staff will not satisfy Article 9 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital (domicile must coincide with the effective management and administration or the principal place of business) and exposes the company to corrective domicile reassignment by the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) under Article 48.3 of Ley 58/2003 (LGT). For the ISIC 4329 / NAICS 238310 activity, the registered office may be a central administrative office provided the operational workshop or yard is separately permitted under municipal opening-license rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk: less than 2% probability of an unannounced inspection at the pre-incorporation stage; approximately 8–10% likelihood of an AEAT census verification visit to the registered office within the first 12 months of active invoicing; up to 15% municipal planning and occupancy inspection in the first 18 months where the registered office contains an operational workshop or material storage; no mandatory physical inspection is required before registration for this non-licensed low-risk industrial contracting line of business.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Madrid and Barcelona market benchmark for a cross-border S.L. incorporation package with foreign corporate shareholders

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Provisional Corporate Tax ID — NIF Provisional — Electronic Processing through the CUSA Notarial Platform
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary (CUSA platform) and Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Municipal Opening Communication or License — Comunicación Previa de Apertura / Licencia de Apertura for the Administrative Office or Workshop

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Regulated Bank Onboarding and AML Client Acceptance File — verification of identity, corporate documentation, PEP/sanctions screening evidence, source of funds

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Arts. 4, 20-34 and 210-211 on incorporation, registered office, share capital, general meeting and directors); implemented by Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil), Ley 14/2013 de apoyo a los emprendedores (CIRCE/DUE single-window) and Ley 18/2022 de creación y crecimiento de empresas (the EUR 1 capital option).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (for the negative denomination certificate) and the competent Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office province (for inscription of the deed), with the Notary of the registered-office municipality; all coordinated through the PAE/CIRCE single window under the Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura pública de constitución (public deed of incorporation) filed for inscription in the hoja registral of the Registro Mercantil under Art. 20 LSC, with subsequent publication in the Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum registered capital is EUR 3,000 (Art. 4 LSC), fully subscribed and paid in cash at execution of the deed, evidenced by a certificate of deposit issued by a Spanish credit institution. Under the Crea y Crece regime, an SL may be formed with EUR 1 of capital if the Bylaws include the obligation to apply profits to the legal reserve until capital plus reserves reach EUR 3,000; the capital cannot be distributed or withdrawn before registration, and any later reduction below the statutory minimum requires judicial approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST GENERAL RESOLUTIONS OF THE INCORPORATORS OF [●] SL. 1. Share subscription and capitalisation: the incorporators approve the public deed of incorporation, confirm the EUR 3,000 registered capital fully subscribed and paid in cash, and accept their share allotments under Bylaw Article 4. 2. Registered office: [●] is adopted as the statutory head office, centre of administration and fiscal domicile. 3. Officers: [Name] is appointed sole Administrator for an indefinite term with Bylaw Article 9 powers, expressly authorised to obtain the provisional NIF, apply for commercial registration and BORME publication, and open bank accounts, each action to comply with the Companies Act and Bylaws.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Negative denomination certificate and corporate name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) via the Entrepreneur Service Point (PAE/CIRCE) or its telematic application, Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online for a certificación negativa de denominación social, presenting up to three proposed corporate names in order of preference. The RMC searches the central index and, if no identical or confusingly similar denomination exists, issues the negative certificate, which reserves the name for three months from issue and obliges the incorporators to execute the deed within that term before a notary.
required_dossiers: Completed RMC certification application (electronic form)
Proof of identity and DNI/NIE of the incorporator(s) or legal representative
List of up to three preferred company names in order of preference
Receipt of the official fee settled online
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RMC refuses or suspends the certificate because of an identical prior denomination, file a fresh application with alternative names or appeal within two months by recurso before the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado after the written refusal; pending resolution, reserve two substitute denominations to preserve the three-month validity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the provisional share-capital account and capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution or bank of the incorporators' choice; deposit subject to Banco de España and AML/CFT supervision under Ley 10/2010
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Bring the negative denomination certificate and the draft Bylaws to the bank, open an account in the name of the sociedad en formación, and deposit the full value of the subscribed capital (not less than EUR 3,000) in euros. The bank issues a certificado de depósito identifying the account holder, the amount and the date of availability, which the notary attaches to the deed as evidence of payment.
required_dossiers: Negative denomination certificate
Draft Bylaws or capital-declaration letter
Identification/NIE of the account signatories
AML declaration of source of funds when required by bank policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the credit institution raises a KYC/AML query, complete the enhanced due-diligence documents (source of funds, residence proof, declaration of final beneficial owner) and resubmit; alternatively, make the cash payment directly deliverable to the notary and record it in the deed, or deposit the capital at the Caja General de Depósitos of the Banco de España, all without altering the minimum capital rule.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the public deed of incorporation before a commercial notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the municipality of the registered office (Colegio Notarial); CIRCE/DUE electronic processing where available
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver to the notary the certification of negative denomination, the bank deposit certificate and the draft estatutos. The notary verifies the legal capacity of the incorporators, the lawfulness of the Bylaws and the adequacy of the capital disclosure, then executes the deed before the parties. The notary requests a provisional NIF from the AEAT at the same time and, in the DUE route, electronically transmits the deed and supporting documents to the Registry.
required_dossiers: Negative denomination certificate (original for the notary's file)
Certificate of deposit issued by the credit institution
Draft Bylaws of the SL covering object, registered office, capital, administration and meeting rules under Art. 22 LSC
Passports/NIE of all incorporators and of the appointed sole Administrator
Independent expert report for non-cash contributions, if any, under Art. 73 LSC
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses or delays execution because of defects in documentation or Bylaws, the incorporators may retain another notary or remedy the defect; in the DUE procedure, excessive fees charged are recoverable by refund claim; any defect noted in the advertencias y reservas must be reconciled before the deed is signed to avoid later registry qualification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Settlement of the corporate operations tax (ITP-AJD) and receipt of the provisional NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Gestión Tributaria in the Autonomous Community of the registered office (Form 600 and provisional NIF issuance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 calendar days of the execution of the deed, the incorporators or the administrator submit the self-assessment of the modalidad de operaciones societarias of the ITP-AJD tax (currently 1% of nominal capital, subject to regional rates) using Form 600 in electronic form. The AEAT simultaneously issues the provisional NIF certificate requested with the deed; the paid or exempt liquidation evidence and the provisional NIF must accompany the later registry filing.
required_dossiers: First notarial copy of the deed of incorporation
Form 600 self-assessment with the liquidation calculation
Provisional NIF documentation issued by the AEAT
Power of attorney, if the filing is made by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT rejects or queries the Form 600, submit the corrective declaration under Art. 120.3 LGT within four years and pay any interest; late-filing surcharges may be reduced by voluntary payment; an appeal (recurso de reposición or reclamación económico-administrativa) may be lodged within one month of the contested assessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the company in the Mercantile Registry and BORME publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office, with publication by the Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (Ministry of Justice)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the first copy (copia autorizada) of the deed, the negative denomination certificate, the ITP-AJD payment and the provisional NIF to the Registry. The registrar performs the calificación registral; upon inscription the company acquires legal personality under Art. 33 LSC, and the Registry publishes the incorporation in the BORME and returns the deed with the registration note to the company.
required_dossiers: First notarial copy of the deed of incorporation with its simple copy
Negative denomination certificate
ITP-AJD liquidation or exemption certificate
Provisional NIF certificate
Supplemental bank certificate and Bylaws as required by the Registro Mercantil Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A negative or suspended qualification may be challenged by an administrative appeal before the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado within two months from notification, or by judicial proceedings; if the defects are formal, rectify the deed before the same notary or complete the missing document and resubmit within the adaptation period set by the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Definitive NIF and tax census registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Oficina de Gestión Tributaria corresponding to the tax domicile
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, the entity communicates its definitive incorporation data via the AEAT census declaration (Form 036), attaches the certified extract of the registration, and requests the definitive NIF card. The company also selects the accounting standard, legal representative and compliance regime in the census before invoicing; an electronic certificate should be applied for to perform tax filings.
required_dossiers: Certified extract or certificación literal of the Registry registration
Form 036 census declaration including the definitive NIF section
Identification of the legal representative with DNI/NIE and supporting power
Notarial certificate of incorporation as a backup to the registry extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT waits or rejects the definitive NIF due to mismatched registry data, obtain a new certified extract and resubmit Form 036 as a rectification; where there is a difference with the Registry, the AEAT requires a certificado de concordancia from the Registrar; against any incorrect denial the company may use the preliminary administrative appeal and, if necessary, the reclamación económico-administrativa.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); official e-office: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Spanish SL: (1) obtain provisional NIF (CIF) from AEAT via Form 036 or through the notary before executing the public deed of incorporation; (2) apply for the definitive NIF immediately after filing in the Registro Mercantil; (3) for foreign shareholders or non-resident contractors, obtain a non-resident NIF (NIF-UE for EU residents or NIF 0/2/4/9 series for non-EU) via Form 030/036 with an appointed fiscal representative where required; (4) also register in the Censo de Empresarios before commencing any taxable activity; (5) if intra-Community supplies/exports are expected, apply for the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) and formally enter the VIES census for EC Sales List filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not have a US-style check-the-box election. An SL is irretrievably a Corporate Income Tax (IS) taxpayer on worldwide income. Available statutory elections include: (i) consolidated tax group election under Art. 61 LIS (tax group filing for 75%+ held Spanish subsidiaries), (ii) optional ETVE reduced taxation regime for eligible holding foreign entities, (iii) SICAV/RCF regime and REIT-equivalent SOCIMI elections, (iv) optional special depreciation/amortization elections under fiscal balance sheets, and (v) limited elections under the Spanish hybrid mismatch rules implementing ATAD where bilateral relief is available. Elections are made via Form 036/036 or by filing the annual IS return; no 'check-the-box' shelter from entity-level taxation exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA) – Spanish VAT, Ley 37/1992 (LIVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None – mandatory registration for any taxable person (persona jurídica) carrying out a continuous economic activity in Spanish territory. No de minimis turnover threshold for established entities; Form 036 must be filed before the first supply of goods/services. For non-established EU distance sellers of goods, the €10,000 intra-Community distance threshold applies (Art. 151 LIVA), but for industrial B2B contracting and services no threshold applies. The simplified VAT regime (Régimen Especial Simplificado) is available to small businesses with prior-year turnover ≤ €150,000 for services or ≤ €250,000 for goods, but it does not exempt from registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain mandates phased B2B electronic invoicing under Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece), in force for all Spanish businesses by 2025–2026. Large taxpayers (annual turnover above €6 million) and VAT groups must additionally file transaction-level invoices and accounting records with AEAT under the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) using XML/SOAP/web-service API submissions within 4 calendar days of invoice issuance (8 days for certain direct-debit invoices). Domestic B2B e-invoicing requires interoperable formats (including FacturaE). Beginning 2024, VERI*FACTU verification codes and QR signatura are mandatory for invoices issued to end consumers by modes of transport; Spain does not operate a continuous physical digital stamping system, but SII acts as a near real-time fiscal clearance mechanism cross-matching invoice data with customs declarations and downstream VAT returns.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Spain to destinations outside the EU/Spain are exempt (0%) under Art. 21 LIVA when the goods physically leave the customs territory within 3 months of dispatch. Intra-Community supplies (dispatches to another EU State) to a customer holding a valid VAT identification number are exempt under Art. 25 LIVA, subject to EC Sales List statements. Services directly related to exports, including international transport, loading/unloading, intermediary services, and work performed on goods destined for export, are exempt under Arts. 22–23 LIVA. Services supplied to non-Spanish business customers are generally outside Spanish VAT under the B2B place-of-supply rule (customer establishment), causing reverse charge in the recipient state. The 0% rate is only available upon objective proof that the goods crossed the border or that the service was physically performed outside Spain; mere invoicing at 0% without qualifying and substantiated supplies constitutes a VAT liability and refund clawback.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/SAD) stamped or PCB-released by Spanish Customs
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR transport document evidencing physical departure from Spanish/EU territory
Commercial Invoice with Incoterms, quantities, goods description and destination
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 or BicWire bank transfer confirmation showing payment from the foreign buyer (where applicable)
Proof of foreign VAT identification number (VIES validation or EU VAT ID certificate) for intra-Community zero-rated supplies
Signed delivery acceptance or service completion certificate for refractory masonry works performed on exported industrial boilers
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT scrutinizes export zero-rating against DUA data, SII invoice records, and bank payment flows. If export proof is missing or inconsistent, the entire VAT is retroactively assessed at the 21% general rate plus late-payment interest (Art. 26 LGT). Penalties for incorrect invoices and false refund claims scale under Arts. 191–195 LGT: minor infringement 50%, serious 50%–100%, and fraudulently obtained refunds expose the taxpayer to aggravated penalties of up to 150%, loss of refund entitlement, and closure of export VAT refund claims. In cases of forged customs documents or circular export schemes, criminal fraud penalties under Arts. 305/308 of the Penal Code (delito contra la Hacienda Pública) apply, imposing fines of two to six times the defrauded amount and imprisonment from 4 to 5 years. All export VAT refund claims are subject to a four-year prescription and may be clawed back ex post with interest and surcharges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) as the national central bank and competent supervisory authority for payment services and prudential conduct, in coordination with the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise (Secretaría de Estado de Economía y Apoyo a la Empresa) for foreign investment statistical registration, and the Directorate General for International Trade and Investment (Secretaría de Estado de Comercio) for the regulatory foreign investment register (Registro de Inversiones Exteriores). SEPBLAC (Financial Intelligence Unit of Spain) acts as the AML/CFT enforcement body. As Spain is a Eurosystem member, monetary policy and TARGET2 liquidity infrastructure are jointly administered by the European Central Bank (ECB).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) is fully convertible under the Capital Free Movement framework of Articles 63-66 TFEU. Spain maintains no general exchange controls, no prior capital-clearance licences for ordinary current-account operations, and no restrictions on profit or dividend remittance from a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL). Foreign direct investment in a Spanish SL is open to non-residents without ministerial approval except: (i) a post-closing statistical declaration to the Banco de España foreign investment loose-leaf register is always required, and (ii) prior authorization under the suspension regime of Law 19/2003 (as amended by Real Decreto 571/2023 and Regulation (EU) 2019/452) applies only if the non-EU/EFTA investor acquires, directly or indirectly, a controlling stake in a Spanish undertaking operating in defence, dual-use, critical energy infrastructure, technology, and other strategically reserved sectors. Refractory masonry contracting (ISIC 4329) is not a reserved sector. Dividend distribution is freely permissible subject to ordinary corporate income tax (25% general rate for an SL), Dividend Withholding Tax (19% domestic withholding for non-resident shareholders, reduced under Spanish treaty networks), and statutory audit/legal reserve constraints. No foreign-currency conversion is required for dividend remittances because the SL's functional and operating currency is the EUR.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Spain abolished all mandatory export-proceeds surrender and repatriation swap obligations for EUR payments. Cross-border receipts for export of services or disbursement-funded contractor payments may remain in EUR or foreign currency without conversion mandate. The only ongoing requirements are: (i) filing the statistical balance-of-payments declaration via the Banco de España financial register for cross-border transactions above the applicable de-minimis thresholds (EUR 12,500 for a single transaction, or EUR 50,000 aggregate per year from same counterparty, unless otherwise waived), and (ii) compliance with the general prohibition on cash payments exceeding EUR 2,500 for business-to-business transactions and EUR 10,000 where at least one party acts in a non-entrepreneurial capacity. On inbound payment from a foreign client, the contractor must retain the MT103/SWIFT evidence and issue an export invoice (factura de exportación) to substantiate the balance-of-payments entry; no exchange surrender or forced conversion applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Cuenta de Depósito de Capital) and Operational Account (Cuenta Operativa)
Capital Escrow Account and Multi-currency Operational Account with FX forward desk
Operational Account, Construction Escrow Sub-accounts, and Aval (Bank Guarantee) facility
Operational Account and Trade-Clearing Account for documentary LCs
Operational Account for relationship-management convenience; limited LC and guarantee desk for small contractors

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with substantial legal constraints. Offshore FinTech and Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) may offer payment accounts and execute MT103-equivalent euro transfers in Spain only if properly passporting under the EU single-passport mechanism of Royal Decree-Law 19/2018 (PSD2) and Law 21/2011 for electronic money. Any third-country EMI (e.g., unlicensed UK, US, or Caribbean digital bank) without a Spanish Bank of Spain payment-institution licence or an EU/EEA home-state passport cannot legally onboard the SL for operational treasury. EMIs usable for the Spanish contractor include EU-authorised entities (e.g., licensed under PSD2) that can provide euro IBANs, SEPA CT, and FX conversion; however, EMIs generally cannot issue Spanish bank guarantees (avales), performance bonds, commercial letters of credit, or structured FX hedging products. For a refractory contracting business executing progress-wire disbursements and trade payments for kiln materials, an EMI should be limited to an ancillary float account, not the primary treasury rail. Recommended primary tier: Tier 1 Spanish bank; secondary tier: Fully regulated EU EMI with passport notification to Banco de España.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Law 10/2010 (Spanish AML Law) and Banco de España Circular 3/2022 do not statutorily require a physical branch visit from all directors; remote onboarding is permitted if the bank employs a reliable independent electronic identification mechanism (video-identification with biometric verification) and receives certified or notarially authenticated corporate documents. However, in practical execution, all leading Spanish Tier 1 banks require at least one statutory legal representative or director with an appointed power of attorney to appear physically at a Spanish branch, or to accept a notarised general-power-of-attorney granted to a local representative (apoderado) who must be identified and sign the account-opening file. Once the account is opened, all subsequent operations (wires, LC issuance, FX forwards, tax authority links) are executed remotely. For a non-EU shareholder or director, an apostilled certified copy of passport and proof of address, plus the SL's notarial deed and registered tax identity certificate (CIF/NIF), are needed before interview calibration. Physical presence is therefore de facto required in the form of an identifiable local representative if no director can travel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed or unclear Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) chain through the foreign shareholder of the SL, in particular when the shareholder is in an offshore jurisdiction or exhibits layered holding structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO declaration (declaración de titular real) submitted to Banco de España Registry; apostilled certificate of incorporation and memorandum of each holding layer; scan of passport pages of every natural-person UBO above 25% capital and control; 3-year audited or accountant-prepared financial statements; tax residence certificate; sworn CFG (source of wealth) letter; annual business plan and a Spanish-site lease/employment payroll evidence demonstrating economic substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital escrow or high-value progress wire referencing a large payment (exceeding EUR 100,000) to a newly established SL with no trading history, particularly if the capital contribution is paid in a lump sum from a foreign juridical person without a clear commercial link.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised capital-increase deed (escritura de ampliación de capital) and bank deposit certificate; loan-to-profit contract if capital is supplied as participative shareholder loan; official SWIFT MT103 and bank reference letter from the remitting institution identifying the account holder, account number, and beneficiary; legalised invoice or order from a named industrial clients; supporting bill of quantities or purchase order for refractory boiler works; compliance declaration under Law 10/2010; tax identification certificate (CIF activo) and NIE of the appointing representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments routed through or to high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions (e.g., third-country procurement of refractory ceramic materials, transit through Latin American hubs), triggering PEP/sanction and embargo screening automated alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate AML compliance manual and sanctions-screening procedure; beneficial-owner and jurisdiction-risk questionnaire for all counterparties; purchase orders and Bills of Lading evidencing final use of materials at specific refinery or boiler site; original commercial contracts with end-user and countries-of-transit disclosure; voluntary self-certification of non-affiliation with sanctioned parties; LOC licensing and dual-use classification memo if any technical article is flagged; proof of registration in the Registro Mercantil and CIF.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mixing of shareholder funds, third-party investor funds, and trade advance disbursement in a single account without contract chain, creating a 'payment anonymisation' red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dedicated escrow or work-specific sub-account agreements for each project; notarised shareholder loan agreements (préstamos participativos) precisely stating purpose and interest rate; authenticated client contract with milestone schedule and approved engineers' certificates; bank-stamped and tax-file-aligned nominal flow chart linking each inbound wire to a specific invoice and outbound vendor payment; sworn statement from the statutory auditor of the SL; SEBPLAC-compliant transaction monitoring records.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the Spanish SL, a non-resident shareholder's capital increase or initial contribution must be executed as a bank-to-bank electronic transfer (no cash) in EUR via SEPA or via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's account. The transfer must specify: (i) beneficiary: the Spanish SL with its unique tax code (NIF/CIF) and Spanish IBAN; (ii) SWIFT purpose code using the EU standard 'EQUITY' or ISO 20022 Remittance Information identifying 'FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT - INCREASE IN CAPITAL'; and (iii) the Spanish counterparty statistical classification 'D.1' for foreign direct investment as required by Banco de España Balance of Payments. After execution, the company must file the mandatory foreign-investment statistical declaration with the Banco de España (form D-1A in the loose-leaf register) using the CIF/NIF of the investor; Real Decreto 571/2023 currently imposes a post-investment declaration obligation without prior authorisation because the activity is non-strategic. The funds may be credited to a temporary Capital Escrow Account (in Spain called 'cuenta de cobros y pagos' or capital deposit account) of the notary handling the capital increase; after notarisation of the deed, the funds are transferred to the company's operative current account. Banks require a statement of source of funds and a confirmation that the operation is linked to the SL statutory objects. No additional exchange-control permission is required for EUR entry.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Commercial suppliers for refractory bricks, ceramic fibre, insulating materials and kiln spare parts are usually settled with: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) via the T2/TARGET2 system for euro payments to EEA vendors, using the counterparty's IBAN; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA suppliers (e.g., China, Germany, Turkey, Latin America), with full remittance information and a reference to the underlying commercial invoice; (iii) Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) under URC 522 where the contractor seeks payment security against shipping documents; and (iv) Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) under UCP 600/URDG 758 for high-value import of refractory material, issued by the Spanish bank at the contractor's request and commonly preferred by the client or SC. For disbursement to the client's own subcontractors in Spain or EU, the contractor uses SEPA CT with tax-file matching of the supplier's CIF/NIF. For milestones from a Latin American employer, the Spanish bank may add a confirmation onto an L/C in USD or EUR; settlement is then made by the issuing bank through correspondent banking rails (e.g., New York, London, or Madrid clearing). All relevant balance-of-payments declarations for cross-border payments above the disclosure thresholds must be filed by the bank on behalf of the SL unless the SL exercises the direct reporting option. Spain's 'Avales' (on-demand guarantees) are available via the Tier 1 bank to energise progress payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD Forward Contract (Seguro de Cambio) with a Spanish credit institution or an EMIR-compliant counterparty - permissible without Bank of Spain authorisation.
Outright EUR/CLP, EUR/MXN and EUR/ARS Forwards for Latin American project currencies, entered into by an authorised Spanish bank desk.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on Latin American restricted currencies (e.g., Argentine peso, Peruvian sol, Chilean peso where offshore delivery is impractical) executed with an EEA-licensed broker, subject to EMIR real-time trade reporting and margining where applicable.

Cross-Currency Swaps (EUR-Foreign Currency) for long-term construction receivables or financing flows in USD/CLP, under ISDA Master Agreement with mandatory EMIR regulatory trade repository reporting and mandatory clearing if exempt thresholds exceeded (typically green-for-clearing derivatives).

FX Options (EUR Calls / Puts on USD and MXN or CLP) for conditional hedging of high-value progress payments, purchased at premium only, not permitted for speculative purposes absent a commercial underlying, and reported under EMIR (EU) 648/2012.

Implicit Corss-Currency Hedging via pre-export finance or BPO (Bank Payment Obligation) confirming a future trade settlement - permissible as a structured treasury product, not an uncovered derivative.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Management prepares accounts within 3 months after year-end; shareholders approve within 6 months; deposit within 1 month after approval. For a 31 December year-end, the normal deposit deadline is 30 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure may apply after 1 year from the filing deadline. Administrative fines generally range from approximately EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, with higher limits for larger companies. Spain does not generally impose automatic administrative strike-off solely for late accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry and the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership, as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Beneficial ownership information must be maintained and updated when changes occur. The beneficial ownership declaration is generally filed with the annual accounts, including confirmation where required by the filing form.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or provide accurate beneficial ownership information may result in registry filing rejection, registry closure, administrative penalties under anti-money-laundering legislation, and director liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a 31 December year-end, the normal filing window is 1 to 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties and late-payment interest apply. Where tax is payable, penalties are generally calculated by reference to the unpaid tax, with increased sanctions for concealment or repeated non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Electronic legalization of accounting books, minute books, the register of members, and applicable sole-shareholder contracts within 4 months after the financial year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the normal deadline is 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted legalization can impair evidentiary value, generate registry compliance issues, and contribute to administrative sanctions or registry closure where connected statutory filings are also overdue.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual value added tax return (Modelo 390), where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally filed from 1 to 30 January following the calendar year, unless the company is exempt from the annual summary return or is subject to an alternative reporting regime.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties apply even where no tax is payable. Additional interest and tax assessments may arise where the return omits or understates taxable transactions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is generally mandatory when a company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets of EUR 4 million, net annual turnover of EUR 8 million, or average workforce of 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory for specified regulated, public-interest, consolidated, or legally designated entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad). IFRS is generally permitted for certain consolidated accounts and required for qualifying listed or regulated groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must identify, verify, retain, and update its ultimate beneficial ownership information. Changes must be reflected without undue delay, and the annual accounts filing generally includes the required beneficial ownership declaration or confirmation. Transfers of shares must be recorded in the register of members and supported by the applicable transfer documentation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Sole-Shareholder Contracts, where applicable

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly created eligible SL entities benefit from a 15% reduced rate on the first EUR 300,000 of positive tax base during the first two tax periods in which taxable base is positive. Additional incentives include an R&D tax credit of 42% of eligible R&D expenses and 20% of technological innovation expenses; capitalization reserve allowance of 10% of retained profits limited to 10% of the taxable base; and a leveling reserve allowance for entities with net turnover below EUR 10 million, allowing a tax base reduction of up to EUR 1 million per year.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory time limit); large taxpayers may be subject to annual offset limits of 50% or 25% of the positive tax base depending on net turnover.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 – Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades); filed electronically through the AEAT Sede Electrónica using a digital certificate or Cl@ve PIN.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 25 calendar days after the six-month period following the end of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year SL, the filing window is 1–25 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF and legal identity of the taxpayer, including name and commercial register data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Permanent establishments must enter the Spanish NIF assigned to the PE and attach the foreign entity's registration details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit (resultado contable) for the fiscal year before corporate income tax, determined under Spanish GAAP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE records only the profit and loss attributable to its Spanish operations; general administrative expenses must be allocated proportionally.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base after permanent and temporary adjustments, offsetting of prior tax losses, and application of capitalization or leveling reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same adjustments to PE income sourced from Spain; Spanish PE tax losses must be tracked separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross corporate tax liability (cuota íntegra) computed at 25%, or 15% for newly created eligible entities on the first EUR 300,000 of positive tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The same rate schedule applies; treaty relief, where available, is claimed in this section to reduce gross tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable (cuota líquida) after tax credits, double-taxation relief, withholding credits, and quarterly prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the relevant treaty relief certificate, Form 210 refund claim, and documentation proving beneficial ownership if excess withholding is to be recovered.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior requirement under Art. 27 LGT: progressive surcharge of 5% (within 3 months), 10% (within 6 months), 15% (within 12 months), or 20% (after 12 months) of the amount due. Advanced filing after administrative notice: fixed penalty of EUR 150–600 plus EUR 120 for each affected box. Late-payment interest accrues at the statutory rate (3.75% in 2024).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% for EU/EEA residents and residents of countries with an effective exchange of information; 24% for other non-residents. Treaty rates may reduce the rate to 0%, 5%, or 10% depending on shareholding and treaty provisions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority and submit it to the Spanish paying entity before distribution. The Spanish entity then applies the reduced withholding and reports it in the relevant withholding return (Modelo 216). If the statutory rate was applied, the non-resident may file Form 210 to claim a refund, attaching the TRC, evidence of shareholding period, and, where required by the treaty, proof of economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 19% for EU/EEA residents and treaty-protected lenders, 24% for others; the EU Interest and Royalties Directive may reduce the rate to 0% for associated EU companies meeting the 25% shareholding and 2-year holding requirement. Royalties: statutory 24%; treaty rates commonly 5% or 10%; EU Directive royalty exemption may apply to EU associated enterprises with qualifying shareholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Spanish Local File and Master File obligations apply when the Spanish entity's net turnover in the preceding tax year exceeds EUR 10 million. For entities below EUR 10 million, simplified documentation may be required when aggregate related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000 in the tax period. Documentation is also mandatory, regardless of turnover, for transactions with entities resident in tax havens.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not impose UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but general substance requirements apply. A Spanish SL must maintain a real registered office, effective management, and demonstrable personnel and commercial operations. Anti-abuse tools include the General Anti-Abuse Rule (Art. 15 LGT), CFC rules (Art. 100 LIS), the interest limitation rule (Art. 16 LIS), and the substance-over-form doctrine under Art. 13 LIS. A shell company without actual refractory masonry activity may be recharacterised as a transparent entity for tax purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Criminal Tax Fraud (Defraudación Tributaria)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underreporting revenue or overstating deductible expenses, including use of false invoices for refractory materials or subcontracting, where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative serious penalty of 50%–150% of the evaded amount under Art. 191 LGT; if the criminal threshold is exceeded, Criminal Code Art. 305 imposes imprisonment of 1–5 years and a fine of 50%–100% of the defrauded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be declared jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt under Art. 42.2.b LGT; criminal conviction may lead to civil restitution, travel bans, imprisonment, and disqualification from managing companies.
